lessons.title: Encryption is a key policy
lessons.why: A customer-managed key you created and then forgot to share with Connect is an outage, not a security win.
paras: Recordings and exported reports can use a customer-managed key. The key policy must allow the Connect service role to generate data keys and decrypt. CloudTrail should record key use. Rotation is available and does not re-encrypt old objects by itself.
TLS covers the CCP and the APIs in transit. That does not encrypt the recording at rest. Those are separate controls.
points: Test a recording end to end after you change the key.
A replica Region needs a key strategy you have actually written down.
Do not use the same key for recordings and for unrelated application secrets if your blast radius matters.
Access to the bucket and access to the key are both required to listen.
lessons.mistake: Enabling the key in the console and not calling a test number.

lessons.title: SAML, least privilege, and the admin you forgot
lessons.why: Federation does not remove the need for a break-glass admin, and it does not make that admin safe.
paras: Use SAML for agents. Keep one local emergency admin whose password is vaulted. Security profiles should split flow editors, user admins, recording listeners, and people who may export contacts.
IAM for builders should be a role they assume, with the instance ARN, not a long-lived key in a flow.
points: Review security profiles when someone changes jobs.
Recording access is a security profile permission. Treat it like access to the conversation, because it is.
Global Resiliency sign-in uses an extra endpoint. The IdP and the firewall both need it.

lessons.title: Quotas are a project plan
lessons.why: The default numbers in the docs are for new accounts. Your account can be lower because defaults have changed over the years.
paras: You must create the instance before you can ask for a raise. Small raises can be hours. Large ones can take three weeks. A worldwide raise can take months. The quota page says this plainly.
Some quotas are not adjustable: 50 agent statuses, 50 task templates, 5 primary attributes on a data table, the 90-day email expiry ceiling.
points: Account-level quotas and resource-level quotas raise differently.
CLI 2.13.20 or newer is required for some resource-level quota calls.
Campaign concurrency and external voice connectors start at 0.
lessons.mistake: Discovering the call quota during the marketing launch.

number.n: Plan on that, not on an hour

lessons.title: How to talk about the price without inventing it
lessons.why: The rate card is public and dated. An estimate that hides the date is a guess.
paras: As of the appendix read for this campus on 14 October 2026, Connect Customer voice is 0.038 USD per minute plus telephony, chat is 0.010 USD per message, email is 0.080 USD, and SMS or third-party messaging is 0.014 USD per message. Customer Basic voice is 0.018 USD per minute plus telephony. US DID telephony in the Oregon example is 0.0022 USD inbound and 0.0048 USD outbound, plus 0.030 USD per day.

Taxes, surcharges, and country rates that are not in that example are extra. Lex speech requests in the Connect Customer example are 0 USD. Live Sync is 0.01 USD per minute and not billed through 30 November 2026. This campus will not invent a toll-free per-minute rate.
points: Say which product form you priced.
A 7-minute call is not 7 times a rounded minute if the voice charge is per second. Telephony in the example still has a 60 second minimum.
The estimator in the lab stamps the date on every result.
Seats are not the unit. There is no seat license in this rate card.
lessons.mistake: A single blended 'per minute' number with no telephony and no date.
